quick.summary: Why building exactly what you are asked for usually backfires.
quick.takeaway: Diagnose the problem before you design a solution.

beats.line: Sales wants a huge buy button. Nobody clicks it today. Why bother?
Because they think size is the issue. But is it really?
If your arm hurts, a doctor does not just wrap it in a cast.
Right, they check for a broken bone first.
Exactly. We call this root cause analysis.
Can I just say find the real problem?
If the price is hidden, a bigger button will not help anyone.
So I should ask why they want it bigger before designing anything.

quiz.question: Your team is asked to redesign a slow dashboard. What is the first step?
options: Find out why it feels slow to users.
Add a loading animation to mask the wait.
Remove half the charts to speed it up.
Move the dashboard to a faster server.
quiz.explanation: You must diagnose the real problem before prescribing a design solution.

quiz.question: Finding the real problem means jumping straight to the easiest fix.
quiz.explanation: It means the opposite. You pause to figure out why the problem is happening in the first place.
